steps.text: Beat butter, peanut butter, white sugar, and brown sugar with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth; beat in eggs.

Sift flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt into a separate bowl; stir into butter mixture until dough is just combined. Chill cookie dough in the refrigerator for 1 hour to make it easier to work with.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Roll dough into 1-inch balls and place 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheets. Flatten each ball with a fork, making a crisscross pattern.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden, about 7 to 10 minutes.
Cool on the baking sheets briefly before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Peanut Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These peanut butter cookies are soft, chewy, and absolutely delicious! Easy to make with smooth or crunchy peanut butter for a crowd-pleasing treat.

video.description: In this video, Nicole shows you how to make the ultimate comfort snack, classic peanut butter cookies. This decadent dessert recipe mixes together the cookie dough by using peanut butter and other common pantry items like sugar and flour. After the dough has been mixed and chilled in the fridge, roll it into individual balls and imprint the vintage fork marks into the each cookie. They’re soft, chewy, and the perfect cookies to enjoy with a glass of milk!

review.reviewBody: I had read on here that people were having trouble with the cookie being too thin, so I added a 1/2 cup more flour, and also 1/2 more peanut butter. the cookie came out great! also added 1 teaspoon vanilla.

Thank you Shirley! This is a fabulous recipe. After reading some very helpful comments, I made a few minor changes. Increased peanut butter to 1 1/2 cups, added an additional 1/4 cup flour, baked at 350 degrees for 9-10 minutes. After forming the dough into balls, I dipped them in sugar and with sugar side up, gently created a criss-cross pattern on top. The cookies are well balanced--crispy edges, chewy centers. Delicate peanut butter flavor. My whole family loved them!!

These cookies were for sure the best Peanut Butter cookies I ever made. I too added just a little more flour and a little more Peanut Butter. I made 2 dozen cookies with them and they were a hit. I made them super soft and gooey. Pull them out of the oven even when they are soft, and let them cool, they will be just the right crispiness on top but soft on the inside. I think I baked my cookies for about 6 or 7 minutes. 

Good luck and enjoy!

I love these cookies! I was out of crunchy PB, so I used creamy, also didn't have unsalted butter, so used the salted and left out the 1/2 tsp. salt. Also, mine took exactly 10 minutes to bake. My kids loved them!!

As is the recipe is 4 stars. I would have given it 5 stars if I hadn't had to make some changes. I followed the suggestions of others and added 1/4 c. extra flour and 1/4 c. extra peanut butter, and put 1 t. vanilla in. I rolled them in sugar before pressing with a fork. I baked them at 350 for 9 minutes. Thanks for a good base recipe.

This is a great recipe! My recommendationns are as follow: Cook for 8 minutes on 350. Add 1/4C more peanut butter. Don't flatten the cookies down too much unless you want a crunchy cookie. Substatute a small amount of oil for butter for a more moist cookie. And of course....add a couple handfulls of chocolate chips! This recipes was really delightful!

I have been using this recipe since I was a litle girl and first began baking! My best friend's Mom made them for us and I thought they were the best cookie around. My "twist" to the recipe is rolling each ball in granulated sugar before flattening with a fork and baking. It really adds to the final results and everyone loves them.

Love this recipe... And yeah ... I made minor adjustments the more times I made it. Peanut butter increased to 1 1/2 cups and flour to 2 3/4 cups. And then a time or two ago, I made the mistake of not creaming the sugars into the butters. Oh noo... Instead, I put all of the dry ingredients, including the sugars, into one container and combined them, and then after creaming the butters and eggs, folded in all the dry at once. It turned out so good, I kept doing like that. Also, I didn't need to cool it off, you can immediately ball it up, fork it down, sprinkle sugar on them, and baked for 9 1/2 minutes. Voila!

Love love love these peanut butter cookies!! They are the epitome of chewy, peanut buttery goodness! I halved the recipe, and still used a heaped 2/3 cup of peanut butter (smooth peanut butter, not crunchy--and I might try adding even more next time!). I also left the salt amount at 1/2 tsp for a half batch, and added about a teaspoon of vanilla plus a 1/4 tsp almond extract. Whenever my mom and grandma would make peanut butter cookies, they always rolled them in white sugar before baking---so I did the same thing with these, and would do it that way every time! I love the extra little hit of sweetness and crunch that sugar on the outside gives. I got exactly 24 cookies out of a half batch, and they were perfectly baked in 10 minutes. Thank you for sharing your recipe--these cookies are delicious nostalgia!

I made these for thanksgiving. They spread SO MUCH! I rolled these things absolutely minuscule, smaller than an inch in diameter. They were so sticky, I had to grease my fork to do the criss cross, and that’s after 1 1/2 hours in the fridge. I admit, that may have contributed to the spreading, but when I pulled them out of the oven, they were very puffy and large. I thought, ‘well, they may have spread over the whole sheet, but at least they’re thick!’ NO! They deflated to about two centimetres tall MAX! And what was once less than an inch in diameter expanded to bigger than my palm! The criss cross design was completely gone.However, they taste delicious! The crunchy peanut butter adds a texture I didn’t know I needed! I added a splash of vanilla extract and about 1/2 tsp of cocoa powder. I think next time I’ll add more flour. I baked for 10 minutes, and they came out soft and chewy in the middle with a crunchy border.EDIT: This recipe is a copy of one found on the label of “Kraft Heinz Crunchy peanut butter”, with a few twists such as a changed amount of baking soda, and chilling the dough. Other than that, it is the same. No where here does it say that the recipe is from Kraft. If this is just a coincidence, my apologies for causing confusion.

I decided to take a chance and not add any extra flour or peanut butter like many others had suggested. I did add a tsp vanilla, made sure my butter and eggs were room temp, chilled the dough for an hour, and rolled the cookie dough balls in sugar before pressing. I used an actual 1" cookie scoop (I think the standard is more like 1.5") and pressed them lightly to be about 1.5" in diameter. I fit 15 per standard cookie sheet, and they came out about 2" wide, with barely any overlapping edges. Baked for about 9-10 min and came out perfect. Ended up with 72 cookies, and that was with some snacking on the dough... Cuz, you know, you have to sample it!
Love, love, love this cookie recipe! My only modification: a teaspoon of vanilla extract. It seems to give the cookies more flavor and depth. This recipe is my go-to!
I made no changes on the first batch but the second batch I mixed in 1 cup of S/s chocolate chips.
It's amazing. Everyone loved them
I love how delicious this recipe taste. Yummy chewy cookies. And great to freeze!!!
I added an extra egg yolk, bumped the PB to 350g and used 380g of flour. Also used 1-1/4 tsp of baking soda and 1-1/4 tsp of baking powder.
I have been making these for years and my family loves them

A few more ingredients, but a whole lot better than a previous peanut butter cookie recipe I used. Chilling the batter was a great idea because I can make enough for a batch and refrigerate the rest. Thank you!
I reduced the sugar by 1/4 and added a bit more natural smooth peanut butter . Also mixed in chocolate and butterscotch chips
Perfect! My grandchildren loved them!
